newsitem.title: USA: Tyco to buy ATT submarine systems unit.
newsitem.headline: Tyco to buy ATT submarine systems unit.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd said Friday it had entered into an agreement to buy AT&T Corp's submarine systems business for about $850 million.
The unit, AT&T Submarine Systems Inc, makes undersea fiber optic telecommunication cable systems.
Tyco, a diversified commercial and industrial manufacturer, said it projects the unit's 1997 revenues at about $1 billion.

L. Dennis Kozlowski, Tyco chairman and chief executive officer, said the deal would make Tyco the world's only fully integrated single source "for everything from cable system design to manufacturing to installation and maintenance."
"The acquisition will have an immediate positive impact on our earnings, as well as providing substantial long-term benefits to Tyco," he said.

John Walter, AT&T president and chief operating officer, said the sale of the submarine systems business would help ensure that AT&T's portfolio includes only businesses important to its communications services strategy.
The move enables AT&T to redeploy its assets into new investment opportunities while continuing to have access to AT&T Submarine Systems Inc (SSI) technologies as a customer, he added.

"Our commitment to our customers is well-served by this move," said William Carter, president of SSI. Carter, along with other SSI executives and some 800 employees, will join Tyco as part of the transaction.
Carter said work on current contracts and the pursuit of future business will continue as planned, and SSI's headquarters will remain in New Jersey.

Tyco operates in more than 50 countries and manufactures disposable medical products, packaging materials, flow-control products, and electrical and electronic components. It also makes and installs fire and safety systems.
